newsitem.title: USA: CBOT sees inflation-indexed notes by April or May.
newsitem.headline: CBOT sees inflation-indexed notes by April or May.

text.p: Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) officials said Wednesday they are targeting an April or May launch for the exchange's proposed inflation-indexed 10-year Treasury note futures and futures-options.
CBOT chairman Patrick Arbor told reporters the board approved the contracts Tuesday and sent them early Wednesday to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission for approval.
The CBOT's move dovetailed with the U.S. Treasury department's auction Wednesday of $7 billion of inflation-protected 10-year notes, its first sale of index-linked government debt securities.

CBOT director Richard Sandor said he anticipates a speedy CFTC approval, possibly within 30 days, so the products could be trading on CBOT's new 60,000-square-foot financial trading floor, which it plans to open February 18, in time for the next Treasury auction.

The CBOT touted the proposed contracts as the first opportunity to trade real yields and synthetic inflation, prospects it expected to attract mainly institutions such as pension funds and dealers rather than retail investors.
"This is really the first opportunity to synthetically trade inflation and hedge against inflation," Sandor said.
Inflation-vulnerable users could take a position in the 10-year note against the inflation-indexed product and create a synthetic consumer price index as a way to hedge, he said.
A U.S. Treasury spokesman said in a statement the proposed futures and options would make it easier for dealers to hedge positions in inflation-indexed securities.
"That, in turn, will aid the development of the inflation-indexed market," he said.

The futures contract will feature physical delivery of inflation-indexed Treasury notes with 6-1/2 to 10 years until maturity and semi-annual coupon payments. It will use a simple conversion factor to calculate invoice price at settlement.

The new futures will offer contract terms similar to other CBOT debt futures, including $100,000 face value, 1/32-point minimum tick size, quarterly trading months and the same trading hours as T-bond futures. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
